topic: Tetris as a latent digital therapeutic mechanism
title: The therapeutic hiding inside Tetris?
creative_basis: Satoshi is physically in an abandoned arcade because Pear Therapeutics and the prescription-digital-therapeutic era color his worldview. The environment is part of the argument, not decoration.

beats.text: I used to believe the future of medicine was prescription software.
Pear Therapeutics made it feel real: FDA-authorized software for addiction and insomnia.
Then reimbursement became the boss fight, and Pear went bankrupt.
Which is why this abandoned arcade bothers me.
While digital health was building therapeutics from scratch, Tetris may already have contained one.
beats.screen_text: WHAT IF THE THERAPEUTIC\nWAS ALREADY INSIDE THE GAME?

beats.text: In Molecular Psychiatry, emergency-department trauma patients were randomized to a brief trauma reminder plus about twenty minutes of Tetris, or a control task. The Tetris group had fewer intrusive memories afterward.
A later randomized healthcare-worker study found a similar signal.
The proposed mechanism is cognitive competition: load visuospatial processing at the right moment, and you may interfere with the imagery that keeps traumatic memories intruding.
Tetris does not treat PTSD. But Pear asked: how do we build therapeutic software?
Maybe the better question is: how much therapeutic machinery is already hiding inside ordinary software?
Drug repurposing — except the drug has been sitting in an arcade since 1984.
